newsitem.title: UK: ING Barings raises 3 Hungarian forecasts, cuts one.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings raises 3 Hungarian forecasts, cuts one.

text.p: ING Barings has raised its earnings per share forecasts for three Hungarian companies and cut one in the November issue of its Eastern European Monthly.
ING Barings raised its EPS forecasts for both 1996 and 1997 for pharmaceuticals Richter, home improvement product maker Graboplast and hotelier Danubius, and lowered for Inter-Europa Bank.
Richter's EPS was raised to 591 forints from 571 forints for 1996 and to 740 forints from 704 forints, due to "excellent third quarter results, fuelled by extraordinary items".
Graboplast's EPS was upgraded to 288 forints from 267 forints for 1996 and to 370 forints from 364 forints for 1997.
Graboplast's upgrading was also the result of the company's good interim results, ING Barings said, adding that the "good third-quarter results were boosted by strong eastern European sales".
Both Richter and Graboplast released their January-September results on November 7.
The investment house raised its EPS forecast for Danubius to 244 forints from 206 forints for 1996 and 277 forints from 272 forints for next year.
It attributed the change to that the delay in the acquisition of Hungaria Szalloda Rt eased pressure on financing costs.

"Danubius had strong third quarter 1996 results, while in the last quarter the hotel chain's margins are likely to be depressed by its bridging loan in order to finance its recent acquisition," it said.
ING Barings left is recommendations unchanged for all the three companies, at "buy" for Richter and at "long-term buy" for Graboplast and Danubius."

Inter-Europa Bank's EPS was reduced to 7,527 forints from 7,864 forints in 1996 and to 9,598 forints from 9,872 next year, because "intensifying competition puts pressure on interest margins," ING Barings said.
ING Barings changed its investment outlook for the bank to "long-term buy" from "buy".
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Richter closed at 7,950 forints, down 150; Graboplast at 4,700 forints, down 100; Danubius at 3,130 forints, down 160 and Inter-Europa at 37,400, down 600.
